was to set up a tent or tabernacle as a house or place where Moses and
Aaron and the elders of the people could commune with Jehovah. This
tabernacle—in reality a portable temple—became more elaborate as rapidly
as the seed of Jacob gained the means and had the time to perfect its
construction. Detailed directions came to Moses by revelation as to the
materials to be used, the ornamentation for its curtains and parts, and the
manner and form of worship attending its use. The tabernacle complex consisted of a large rectangular court in the
western part of which stood a small building or tabernacle. In the eastern
part of the court were an altar for the offering of sacrifices and a laver for
priestly washings. All Israel had access to the court wherein these burnt
offerings were made.
